summary: Iter 215bn - ModalShell chrome consistency testing. All 4 modals (ClassEditor, PlanEditor, AddMember, AdEditor) have correct styling (rounded-2xl/16px, max-h-[90vh], shadow-xl) and all close mechanisms work (X button, ESC key, backdrop click). CRITICAL BUG: Sticky header not working - X close button scrolls out of viewport on modals with long content (ClassEditor, PlanEditor, AdEditor). AddMember modal works correctly as it has less content. Pulse safety verified (/pulse and /pulse-pricing preserve data-brand=pulse).

ui_bugs.issue: Sticky header not working - X close button scrolls out of viewport when modal content is long. Header should stay fixed at top but scrolls with content.

action_items: Fix sticky header in ModalShell - the header with X close button should stay fixed at top when modal content scrolls. Current implementation has 'sticky top-0' but it's not working for modals with long content.
Possible fix: Add 'overflow-hidden' to outer container and create a separate scrollable body container, OR investigate why sticky positioning fails when modal opens with auto-focus on form fields.
critical_code_review_comments: ModalShell line 1953: 'overflow-y-auto' on the modal container should work with 'sticky top-0' on the header, but the sticky positioning is failing. The header scrolls out of view instead of staying fixed.
The issue may be related to browser auto-scrolling to focused form fields when modal opens, which could be pushing the sticky header out of view.

success_rate.frontend: 85% - All close mechanisms work, styling correct, but sticky header bug affects UX
